not-mutated.reason: Throws on missing/invalid frontmatter, but no mutated gate consumes it: wiki-ingest.ts implements its own local parseFrontmatterDocument/renderFrontmatterDocument instead of importing this module. Its one production consumer is repo-page-move.ts (itself not-mutated, below), which imports parseFrontmatterDocument/renderFrontmatterDocument; the page-move tests reach it through the package-name import, not a same-tree import. wiki-write-core.test.ts additionally exercises reconstructFrontmatter, and only its happy path.

validateRenderingPolicy returns unsafe-html findings but no production gate consumes it (only wiki-write-core.test.ts calls it directly). maskCodeContent/maskNonProseContent, the functions the corrections-survival.ts gate does call, are pure content transforms with no rejection path of their own.

splitFrontmatter's error field is the only rejection-shaped output here, and its sole consumer is wiki-lint.ts, itself not-mutated pending relocation. collectWikiPages/collectWikilinks, consumed by the mutated corrections-survival.ts and wiki-ingest.ts, are non-rejecting collection helpers, and findWikilinkSpans (consumed by repo-page-move.ts, itself not-mutated) is the same scan with offsets.
resolveMarkdownLinks' exists signal is consumed only by wiki-lint.ts, itself not-mutated pending relocation; no mutated module reaches this file.

Pure locator for fenced code blocks and inline code spans, with no rejection path of its own: it returns offsets and never throws. Its consumers (markdown-links.ts and wiki-utils.ts) are themselves not-mutated, and their tests reach it through the package-name import rather than a same-tree import. Pinned behaviorally by scripts/markdown-links.test.ts and scripts/wiki-utils.test.ts, and by packages/wiki-write-core/src/code-regions.test.ts, which keeps the rescanning inline-span scan as the reference, compares it on 60,000 weighted bodies and bounds a 1.2 MB line of unmatched openers.

The inline-link scanner behind resolveMarkdownLinks: a linear-time form of the regex it replaced. It is internal (not in the package exports) and its only consumer, markdown-links.ts, is not-mutated. packages/wiki-write-core/src/inline-links.test.ts keeps the old regex and the old resolveMarkdownLinks loop as the reference and compares them on 60,000 seeded lines, 60,000 seeded bodies and every UTF-16 code unit in 16 templates, and bounds the strings CodeQL reported for alerts 46 and 47.

The markdown-link and wiki-link scanner behind normalizeFormattingText: a linear-time form of the regex it replaced. It is internal (not in the package exports) and its only consumer, corrections-survival.ts, is mutated; the tests that kill that module's mutants reach this one through normalizeFormattingText. packages/wiki-write-core/src/link-labels.test.ts keeps the old regex as the reference, compares it on 60,000 seeded strings with the capture groups and through normalizeFormattingText, and bounds adversarial text.

The wiki index entry-line scanner (used by wiki-ingest.ts) and the flow-style `related:` scanner (used by repo-page-move.ts): linear-time forms of the regexes they replaced. It is internal (not in the package exports) and both consumers are not-mutated. packages/wiki-write-core/src/line-scanners.test.ts keeps the old regexes as the reference, compares them on 60,000 seeded documents and 60,000 seeded lines, and bounds adversarial input.

Exported request-time GitHub adapter with no current CI or autonomous-write caller in this repository; only its dedicated tests and the package barrel reference it. Survey routing predicate, not an independent write or promotion authority. runCheck fails closed (onboarded:false) on every error path -- missing env, ENOENT, malformed YAML, and schema failure all resolve to false, never true. Documentation-quality lint for broken relative links. It does not protect a security boundary, autonomous write, persisted trust state, or generated executable artifact; its behavior is adequately covered by conventional tests.

Supply-chain lint failing on any high or critical advisory that `bun audit --json` reports against the installed dependency tree (see PR #3871). Release-time proof, not a gate on content: packs the staged @fro.bot/wiki-write-core package, unpacks the tarball into a scratch node_modules, and spawns npm, tar, node and tsc to resolve, import and type-check every export. Its behavior is spawned processes and the filesystem, so a mutant is only observable through a real build and pack: scripts/wiki-write-core-package.test.ts runs that for real and pins each refusal (a file outside dist/, an export target missing from the tarball, a declaration file that does not type-check) with a negative case, and scripts/verify-wiki-write-core-package.test.ts pins the pack-result parser. Mutating it would run a build, a pack and a type-check per mutant.

CI lint that parses allowedVersions values with Renovate's own versioning API (renovate/dist/modules/versioning, util/string-match) and fails on anything Renovate would reject at lookup time. It protects the published default.json preset from a config-breaking edit, not a security boundary, autonomous write, persisted trust state, or generated executable artifact. Every verdict branch (npm range, regex form, rule-declared non-npm versioning, semver fallback, unknown versioning, non-string, templated skip) and the failing rule naming are asserted directly in scripts/check-renovate-ranges.test.ts. Whether it belongs in stryker.config.json's mutate set is a separate materiality decision, deliberately left open here.

Locates, installs and loads the pinned scratch Renovate for the preset gate (pin parsing, prefix resolution, install-command shape, fail-loud version check). Pin parsing, prefix resolution, install flags and the missing/mismatched-install failures are asserted in scripts/renovate-runtime.test.ts; the real module loading is exercised by its RENOVATE_PREFIX integration test.

Thin CLI over installRenovate in scripts/renovate-runtime.ts: reads the pin, resolves the prefix, installs, prints the prefix. The logic it delegates to is tested there; this file holds no decision of its own.

CI lint orchestrating renovate-config-validator (--strict --no-global) over default.json, .github/renovate.json5 and the version-pinned github> presets they extend, then the allowedVersions range check. The writes of a reconcile run (star sync, survey dispatch with its stagger, the issue queue, labels, auto-close and self-heal). Every failure is non-blocking and logged. Pinned by packages/registry/src/reconcile-repos.test.ts with injected clients. Not in the mutate list: transport glue, and none of it writes to data or main.

The I/O shell of a reconcile run: handleReconcile reads, plans, verifies the data branch, commits to data through commit-metadata, then dispatches, files issues and syncs stars. Pinned end to end by packages/registry/src/reconcile-repos.test.ts and packages/registry/src/reconcile-wiki-rename-guard.test.ts with injected clients. Not in the mutate list because it is an I/O shell around those clients and a scheduled writer to data only.

Test support: the route table, preload arguments and call log of a fake GitHub API for spawned CLI tests. It decides nothing for a gate and has no production importer; its behaviour, including the preload fixture it points at, is pinned by packages/test-kit/src/fake-github.test.ts.

The types, constants and type guards of a coordination goal (ELIGIBLE_OWNERS, FROBOT_COMMENT_AUTHORS, REQUIRED_APPROVER, RECEIPT_SLA_MS, CAS_MAX_RETRIES, the status sets, isGoalStateBody). It holds data and shape checks, no I/O. The guards are exercised through the marker round-trip and parse tests in packages/dispatch/src/cross-repo-dispatch.test.ts, and the constants through the gate, plan and approver tests in the same file. Not in the mutate list: a Stryker run would mostly score literal changes to constants that other modules' decision tables already pin.

Hash, parse, select and serialize of the state marker embedded in a coordination issue's comments. Its decisions (last marker wins, bot-authored markers only, a malformed or hash-less marker is null, a canonical latest-state-only hash) are pinned by the marker round-trip, selectStateMarker and fingerprint tests in packages/dispatch/src/cross-repo-dispatch.test.ts. The marker hash it computes is what every compare-and-swap in dispatch-run.ts compares, and dispatch-plan.ts serializes through it; scripts/dispatch-flows.test.ts parses the markers the real entrypoint writes with extractMarker and scripts the confirm write's read from buildMarkerComment. Not in the mutate list: it never writes to GitHub itself, and a hash or parse regression fails the executors' compare-and-swap tests and those flows.

Text parsing of coordination comments (the planner checklist, the worker receipt with its escape repair) and the three-gate receipt resolver (Fro Bot author, correlation id maps to an item, hash(nonce) equals the stored hash), plus the nonce primitives. Pinned by decision-table tests in packages/dispatch/src/cross-repo-dispatch.test.ts: the checklist grammar, the receipt region and bare-marker forms, escape repair, earliest-receipt-wins, forged-nonce and non-bot receipts, and early receipts. packages/dispatch/src/dispatch-receipts.test.ts pins the receipt-marker scan against the forward walk it replaced on 60,000 seeded bodies and bounds it at 20,000 prefixes. Not in the mutate list: it never writes; the executors that act on its verdicts are in dispatch-run.ts and write only to the coordination issue's marker comment.

The pure planners (registry gate, dispatch plan, snapshot plan) and the prompt safety policy and builder. Pinned by the gate, same-target serialization, snapshot and prompt-safety tests in packages/dispatch/src/cross-repo-dispatch.test.ts. Not in the mutate list: it is pure planning over values the executors pass in, and the executors re-read and re-compare the approval fingerprint before every item.

The executors: runDispatch on an approval and runTrack on a schedule, with the compare-and-swap marker write they share. They dispatch workflows into owner repos and update the coordination issue, never data or main. Pinned end to end by the runDispatch, runTrack and CAS tests in packages/dispatch/src/cross-repo-dispatch.test.ts, against injected clients, and by scripts/dispatch-flows.test.ts through the real entrypoint against a fake GitHub. Not in the mutate list because the module's boundary is its injected clients, so a Stryker run would mostly score transport glue.

GitHub adapters: run and goal-issue lookups, parseTargetTokens and the per-owner client resolver. Pinned by the lookup, token-map and resolver tests in packages/dispatch/src/cross-repo-dispatch.test.ts and, for the 15 s timeout on every client, by scripts/octokit-entrypoints.test.ts. Not in the mutate list: thin wrappers over injected clients.

The production composition of cross-repo-dispatch (the registry read, the per-owner clients, the dispatch and track bodies) and its goke entrypoint. Pinned by the runDispatchCli and runTrackCli composition tests in packages/dispatch/src/cross-repo-dispatch.test.ts, by packages/dispatch/src/dispatch-cli.test.ts for the CLI surface, by packages/dispatch/src/dispatch-cli-env.test.ts for reading only the env the runner supplies, and by scripts/dispatch-flows.test.ts, which spawns the shim. Not in the mutate list: it is I/O wiring, and the decisions it wires are in the modules above.

Plans the repositories Renovate may be dispatched to (the installation's repositories intersected with metadata/renovate.yaml) and dispatches the workflow, skipping a repository whose run is queued or in progress. It writes only workflow_dispatch events and one $GITHUB_OUTPUT line, never data or main. Pinned by packages/dispatch/src/dispatch-renovate.test.ts: the plan, the running-run check, the failure shapes and the missing-input errors. Not in the mutate list: transport glue over an injected client.

The goke entrypoint of dispatch-renovate: `plan` and a no-argument root command, nothing else. Argv that matches neither is a usage error and dispatches nothing. Pinned by packages/dispatch/src/dispatch-renovate-cli.test.ts and, through the shim, by scripts/dispatch-flows.test.ts. Not in the mutate list: it declares two commands, so a mutation run would score only the config object.

Entrypoint shim: it imports main from @fro-bot/dispatch/dispatch-cli and runs it under the entry guard. The behaviour is in packages/dispatch/src/dispatch-*.ts, pinned by packages/dispatch/src/cross-repo-dispatch.test.ts. The shim's surface, including the mode errors, a usage error on unmatched argv and that importing it runs nothing, is pinned by scripts/dispatch-flows.test.ts.

Entrypoint shim: it imports main from @fro-bot/dispatch/dispatch-renovate-cli and runs it under the entry guard. The behaviour is in packages/dispatch/src/dispatch-renovate.ts and dispatch-renovate-cli.ts, each pinned by its own tests. The shim's surface, including a usage error on unmatched argv and that importing it runs nothing, is pinned by scripts/dispatch-flows.test.ts.

The rollout tracker preflight: the Project, tracked-issue, comment and external-signal reads, the snapshot and its hash, the marker parse and the wake decision. It writes nothing to GitHub, `data` or `main`: its only output is one JSON line on stdout that gateway-rollout-tracker.yaml and status-truth.yaml read. Pinned by packages/status-truth/src/rollout-tracker-snapshot.test.ts: the pure functions, the fixture path, the live `gh` and health reads against stub binaries and a local server, and the workflow shape. packages/status-truth/src/rollout-tracker-snapshot-cli.test.ts pins the runner wiring, and scripts/status-truth-flows.test.ts runs the real shim under Bun for the five fields the preflight job reads, a result above 300 KB delivered complete through a pipe, and the failure that makes `jq -e` fail the `if`. Not in the mutate list: it was never mutated, and it decides only whether a tracker agent run wakes.

The goke entrypoint of rollout-tracker-snapshot: one read-only root command that takes no argument, runs the preflight and hands back its exit code. Any argument is a usage error and reads nothing. Pinned by packages/status-truth/src/rollout-tracker-snapshot-cli.test.ts (the config, the exit code and stderr of a run, a thrown error, the usage errors, and that `main` sets `process.exitCode` without calling `process.exit`) and, through the shim, by scripts/status-truth-flows.test.ts. Not in the mutate list: it declares one command, so a mutation run would score only the config object.

Entrypoint shim: it imports main from @fro-bot/status-truth/rollout-tracker-snapshot-cli and runs it under the entry guard. The behaviour is in packages/status-truth/src/rollout-tracker-snapshot.ts, pinned by packages/status-truth/src/rollout-tracker-snapshot.test.ts, which also spawns this shim under Node. The shim's surface, including a usage error on unmatched argv and that importing it runs nothing, is pinned by scripts/status-truth-flows.test.ts.

The shared model of the status-truth loop: the claim kinds and their grammars (CLAIM_KIND_DEFINITIONS), the finding and report types, the report envelope with its schema and fingerprint versions, the claim fingerprint, and validateStatusTruthArtifact, the check the proposals and PR steps run before they plan a write. It does no I/O. Pinned by packages/status-truth/src/status-truth-detect.test.ts: the grammar table, the fingerprint, the report status and eligibility rules, and every rejection of validateStatusTruthArtifact (versions, required fields, prohibited fields, count mismatch). packages/status-truth/src/status-truth-proposals.test.ts and status-truth-prs.test.ts reject an unknown-version report through it before any planning, and scripts/status-truth-flows.test.ts pins the report keys the workflow reads. Not in the mutate list: it was never mutated, and a literal change in a grammar or a version constant fails those tests.

Pure verdicts: classifyClaim, buildProposedCorrection and detectStatusTruthClaims decide whether a claim is current, drifted, unresolved or unsafe, and an unsafe finding carries no identity. Pinned by the classification, correction-text and ordering tests in packages/status-truth/src/status-truth-detect.test.ts, including the private and unavailable resolvers that must never read as drifted. Not in the mutate list: it was never mutated; it proposes, and the public-output gate and the proposals step decide what is written.

Claim extraction: the bounded scan globs and exclusions, the grammars that pull claims out of one document (with the cross-repo suppression of a bare number), the file scan and the scan of current-repo issue bodies and comments that skips the loop's own proposal issues. It reads through injected listers and readers. Pinned by the extraction, exclusion, scan-error and issue-scan tests in packages/status-truth/src/status-truth-detect.test.ts. Not in the mutate list: it was never mutated, and it only produces claims that the resolvers and classifier then judge.

The rollout-tracker compound resolver and the snapshot loader. A claim is compared against the `issue_state` of the matching snapshot item and nothing else, and a snapshot that is absent, malformed or has an invalid item loads as null so the claims stay unresolved. Pinned by the resolver and loader tests in packages/status-truth/src/status-truth-detect.test.ts, which cover every malformed shape, and by scripts/status-truth-flows.test.ts, which passes a snapshot file through the real entrypoint. Not in the mutate list: it was never mutated, and a failed load only leaves claims unresolved.

Live-state resolution with a read-only client: pull requests, issues and releases of the current repository, the publicness proof that must precede any cross-repo identity, and the loop that counts resolver errors. Every request it makes is a GET. Pinned by the resolver, pagination, publicness and error-count tests in packages/status-truth/src/status-truth-detect.test.ts, and by scripts/status-truth-flows.test.ts, which asserts that a real run sends only GETs with the read-only token. Not in the mutate list: its boundary is an injected client, so a Stryker run would mostly score transport glue.

The plan resolvers: plan-status reads a plan file's frontmatter, and plan-consistency audits docs/plans/*.md for a frontmatter status that disagrees with its unit checkboxes. Its bounded corrector and re-verifier are what status-truth-prs.ts writes with, so the drift matrix and the corrector are the contract. Pinned by the frontmatter, checkbox-grammar, drift-matrix, corrector and re-verification tests in packages/status-truth/src/status-truth-detect.test.ts, and by the corrector round trips in packages/status-truth/src/status-truth-prs.test.ts. Not in the mutate list: it was never mutated, and the PR step re-reads the live file and re-verifies the corrected content before any write.

The production composition of status-truth-detect and its goke entrypoint: the preconditions, the scan, the report write and the counts-only summary. It makes only read-only GitHub requests. Pinned by packages/status-truth/src/detect-cli.test.ts (the config, each precondition, the unwritable report, the usage errors and `main`) and by scripts/status-truth-flows.test.ts, which spawns the shim with and without a token and asserts the report keys the summary step reads, the counts-only stdout and that every request is a GET. Not in the mutate list: it is I/O wiring, and the decisions it wires are in the modules above.

Entrypoint shim: it imports main from @fro-bot/status-truth/detect-cli and runs it under the entry guard. The behaviour is in packages/status-truth/src/detect-*.ts and report-model.ts, pinned by packages/status-truth/src/status-truth-detect.test.ts. The shim's surface, including a usage error on unmatched argv and that importing it runs nothing, is pinned by scripts/status-truth-flows.test.ts.

The label vocabulary of the proposal lifecycle: the primary label, the outcome labels, the terminal, resolving and accuracy-signal sets derived from them, and REQUIRED_LABELS, the list the executor confirms before it opens anything. It holds data and does no I/O. Pinned by the lifecycle, terminal-suppression, reopen and label-gate tests in packages/status-truth/src/status-truth-proposals.test.ts, and by scripts/settings-labels-effective-set.test.ts, which compares REQUIRED_LABELS with .github/settings.yml. Not in the mutate list: a Stryker run would mostly score literal changes to label names that those tests already pin.

The hidden markers in a proposal issue body (fingerprint, live state, kind), their builders and parsers, the recovery of a claim kind from an older body, the closed vocabulary of claim kinds that keeps body text out of telemetry keys, and the cooldown after a terminal close. Pinned by the marker round-trip, malformed-marker, kind-recovery and cooldown tests in packages/status-truth/src/status-truth-proposals.test.ts. Not in the mutate list: it was never mutated, it does no I/O, and a regression in a marker pattern fails the planner tests that read the markers back.

The outcome read-model of the existing proposal issues: the classification of one issue into an outcome state and the aggregate counts, overall and per claim kind. It is counts only and never writes. Pinned by the classification table and the aggregate-count tests in packages/status-truth/src/status-truth-proposals.test.ts (every state, conflicting and malformed labels, the per-kind buckets) and by scripts/status-truth-flows.test.ts, which asserts the nine outcome keys the summary step reads. Not in the mutate list: it was never mutated, and it feeds a summary, not a write.

The proposal lifecycle planner (planStatusTruthProposalActions) and the title, body and comment builders: open, update, reopen, close or suppress per fingerprint, same-run deduplication, terminal-label suppression, close-on-clear only after a complete scan, an unknown report version rejected before any planning, and every rendered surface through the public-output gate. Pure: it plans and writes nothing. Pinned by the lifecycle decision tables in packages/status-truth/src/status-truth-proposals.test.ts and, through the real entrypoint, by scripts/status-truth-flows.test.ts. Not in the mutate list: it was never mutated, and the executor performs only the actions it plans, behind a label gate.

The proposal executor and its reads: the label gate (fail closed when any required label is missing), exhaustive pagination of the existing proposal issues, and the planned actions applied to this repository's issues, or only counted in a dry run. A failed action does not stop the rest. It writes issues and labels of one repository, never data or main. Pinned by the executor and fetch tests in packages/status-truth/src/status-truth-proposals.test.ts against injected clients (dry run makes no call, the label gate, 404 and 422 on label creation, each action's failure) and by scripts/status-truth-flows.test.ts against a fake GitHub. Not in the mutate list: its boundary is an injected client, so a Stryker run would mostly score transport glue.

The production composition of status-truth-proposals and its goke entrypoint: the report read and validation, the privacy-token load, the read-only fetch in a dry run and the fail-closed fetch in a live run, the plan, the execute and the counts-only result. A dry run (exactly STATUS_TRUTH_DRY_RUN=true) makes no write; any other value takes the live path, and status-truth.yaml supplies the dry run by default. Pinned by packages/status-truth/src/proposals-cli.test.ts (the config, the preconditions, the usage errors and `main`) and by scripts/status-truth-flows.test.ts, which spawns the shim: the dry run makes zero mutating calls, the live path, the unset-variable behaviour, every exit-1 path and the keys the summary step reads. Not in the mutate list: it is I/O wiring, and the decisions it wires are in the modules above.

Entrypoint shim: it imports main from @fro-bot/status-truth/proposals-cli and runs it under the entry guard. The behaviour is in packages/status-truth/src/proposal-*.ts and proposals-cli.ts, pinned by packages/status-truth/src/status-truth-proposals.test.ts. The shim's surface, including a usage error on unmatched argv that writes nothing even on the live path and that importing it runs nothing, is pinned by scripts/status-truth-flows.test.ts.
